question: Identify the L1_model associated with each model (specified by name and version) that occurs most frequently for each status ('strong' or 'soft'), along with the number of times it occurs. A model has a 'strong' status if, for any of its steps, the maximum test score among non-'Stack' models is less than the 'Stack' model's test score. It has a 'soft' status if the maximum test score among non-'Stack' models equals the 'Stack' model's test score. Count how many times each L1_model is associated with a 'strong' or 'soft' status across all models, and determine which L1_model has the highest occurrence for each status.
sql:
WITH stack_scores AS (
    SELECT name, version, step, test_score AS stack_score
    FROM model_score
    WHERE model = 'Stack'
),
non_stack_max AS (
    SELECT name, version, step, MAX(test_score) AS max_non_stack
    FROM model_score
    WHERE model != 'Stack'
    GROUP BY name, version, step
),
step_status AS (
    SELECT s.name, s.version, s.step,
           CASE WHEN n.max_non_stack < s.stack_score THEN 'strong'
                WHEN n.max_non_stack = s.stack_score THEN 'soft'
                ELSE 'other' END AS status
    FROM stack_scores s
    JOIN non_stack_max n ON s.name = n.name AND s.version = n.version AND s.step = n.step
),
model_status AS (
    SELECT name, version,
           MAX(CASE WHEN status = 'strong' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as has_strong,
           MAX(CASE WHEN status = 'soft' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as has_soft,
           MAX(CASE WHEN status = 'other' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as has_other
    FROM step_status
    GROUP BY name, version
),
model_with_status AS (
    SELECT ms.name, ms.version,
           CASE WHEN ms.has_strong = 1 THEN 'strong'
                WHEN ms.has_strong = 0 AND ms.has_soft = 1 AND ms.has_other = 0 THEN 'soft'
                ELSE NULL END AS model_status,
           m.L1_model
    FROM model_status ms
    JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT name, version, L1_model FROM model) m ON ms.name = m.name AND ms.version = m.version
    WHERE CASE WHEN ms.has_strong = 1 THEN 'strong'
               WHEN ms.has_strong = 0 AND ms.has_soft = 1 AND ms.has_other = 0 THEN 'soft'
               ELSE NULL END IS NOT NULL
),
l1_counts AS (
    SELECT model_status, L1_model, COUNT(*) as cnt
    FROM model_with_status
    GROUP BY model_status, L1_model
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT model_status, L1_model, cnt,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY model_status ORDER BY cnt DESC) as rn
    FROM l1_counts
)
SELECT model_status as status, L1_model, cnt
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
